reason: Selected main tables show model-by-benchmark reversals and a material stronger-interpreter confound.

candidates.title: Test perception-reasoning decomposition per model and benchmark
candidates.rule: For diagram-grounded math, compare direct solving with an interpreter–solver pipeline separately for every intended model and workload before adopting decomposition.
candidates.passage: the smaller Qwen 7B shows a –6.0% drop
candidates.finding: Qwen-2.5-VL 7B improves on Geometry3K, OlympiadBench and We-Math but declines on MathVerse. Gemini-2.0-Flash declines on three benchmarks and improves modestly on We-Math. The abstract overstates consistency; the tables show exceptions.
candidates.conditions: All multi-agent configurations in Table 1 use Gemini-2.0-Flash as interpreter. Results use pass@3, not one-shot accuracy or all-trial reliability.
candidates.limitations: A stronger extra model and added inference are confounded with decomposition. Fixed zero-shot prompts, limited models and quantization constrain generalization. No matched-cost superiority or adaptive router is demonstrated.
candidates.validation_test: At matched cost compare direct solving, repeated direct samples and interpreter–solver variants. Separate interpreter capability from decomposition and report one-shot as well as pass@3 results.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
